question: An events manager is about to hand an end-to-end campaign setup task to Claude in Cowork for the first time, working across her own files and connected tools. What should she do first?
options: A) Choose the largest campaign of the quarter, so the value of the new arrangement is obvious to all.
B) Turn off the automatic checks so that the task can complete without interruption on its first run.
C) Decide which actions in the task a person must approve before they happen, and set that up.
D) Ask Claude to describe how it would approach the task and keep that as the record of the plan.
correct_answers: C) Decide which actions in the task a person must approve before they happen, and set that up.
explanations: Making the first run the biggest campaign maximises the consequences of an untested arrangement. A first outing should be chosen so that mistakes are cheap, not so that success would be impressive.
Removing the checks on a first run is the opposite of prudent. Uninterrupted completion is worth little if the manager cannot see what was done to her files and messages along the way.

Correct. A task that spans files and connected tools will take actions with real consequences, so the first decision is which of those a person must approve. Setting the approval points up front is what keeps the manager in control of the steps that cannot be undone.
A stated plan is a useful reference and worth having, but it is a description rather than a control. The task can still take an action she would not have sanctioned, because nothing stops it to ask.
